IB 2027 · HL · Unit 3

Unit 3: Recursive Problem Solving

HL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

How can a problem solve itself?

This unit focuses on Self-Reference and Decomposition. You will learn how to write functions that call themselves to solve complex problems like sorting (Quicksort) and tree traversal. You will start by tracing the Runtime Stack and finish by mastering the Divide and Conquer strategy.

You'll begin with the anatomy of a recursive method (Base Case vs General Case). Then you'll visualize memory using the Call Stack (Winding/Unwinding), and apply this logic to implement efficient algorithms like Quicksort.

The Anatomy of Recursion

A recursive method has two parts. Without both, it fails:

  • Base Case: The stopping condition (e.g., if n == 0). Stops the infinite loop.
  • General (Recursive) Case: The logic that calls the method again with a smaller input (e.g., return n + Sum(n-1)).
The Call Stack (Memory)

How does the computer remember where it was? It uses a Stack.

  • Winding (Push): Adding a new "Frame" to the stack for each call.
  • Unwinding (Pop): When the Base Case is hit, frames pop off, returning values back up the chain.
Divide & Conquer (Sorting)

Recursion is powerful for breaking big problems into small ones.

  • Quicksort: Pick a pivot, partition the list (smaller left, bigger right), then recurse on both sides.
  • Merge Sort: Split the list in half recursively until size 1, then merge them back in order.
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Recursion A programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem.
Base Case The condition that stops the recursion (prevents an infinite loop).
Recursive Step The part of the function where it calls itself with a modified (usually smaller) parameter.
Call Stack A memory structure that stores 'Stack Frames' for each active function call (tracks local logic).
Stack Overflow A fatal error that occurs when the Call Stack runs out of memory (usually due to a missing Base Case).
Stack Frame A section of the stack dedicated to a single function call, storing its arguments, return address, and local variables.
Pivot The element in Quicksort used to partition the array.
